source_text: Ὁ γοῦν Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἐλέγχει μὲν αὐτὸν ὡς πάντα τὰ ἐκ νόμου μὴ πεπληρωκότα, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀγαπᾷ καὶ ὑπερασπάζεται τῆς ἐν οἷς ἔμαθεν εὐπειθείας, ἀτελῆ δὲ εἶναί φησιν ὡς πρὸς τὴν αἰώνιον ζωήν, ὡς οὐ τέλεια πεπληρωκότα καὶ νόμου μὲν ἐργάτην, ἀργὸν δὲ ζωῆς ἀληθινῆς. καλὰ μὲν οὖν κἀκεῖνα (τίς δ᾿ οὔ φησιν; ἡ γὰρ »ἐντολὴ ἁγία«) ἄχρι παιδαγωγίας τινὸς μετὰ φόβου καὶ προπαιδείας ἐπὶ τὴν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ νομοθεσίαν τὴν ἄκραν καὶ χάριν προχωροῦντα. πλήρωμα δὲ »νόμου Χριστὸς εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι«, οὐχὶ δὲ δούλους ποιῶν ὡς δοῦλος, ἀλλὰ καὶ υἱοὺς καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ συγκληρονόμους τοὺς ἐπιτελοῦντας τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός.
thought_title: Jesus loves the law-keeping rich man but calls him incomplete
orientation: Clement is explaining Jesus' response to the rich man who said he had kept the commandments from his youth.
pass_a_gloss: So Jesus does not reprove him as one who has not fulfilled all the things from the law, but he also loves him and embraces warmly his obedience in the things he learned, but he says he is incomplete as regards eternal life, as one who has not fulfilled perfect things and is a worker of the law but idle in true life. Those things then are good (who says not? for the commandment is holy) up to a certain child-leading with fear and preliminary teaching for those advancing to the supreme legislation of Jesus and grace. But the fulfillment of law is Christ for righteousness to everyone who believes, not making slaves as a slave, but also sons and brothers and co-heirs those who accomplish the will of the father.

choices.why: The compound with ὑπερ- intensifies the embrace; it conveys affectionate approval, not mere acceptance.
Clement contrasts ἀτελῆ with τέλεια in the same sentence; 'incomplete' preserves the root contrast with 'perfect things.'
The Greek term refers to the slave who escorted children; rendering it literally preserves the pedagogical metaphor Clement is using for the law.
Clement uses the abstract noun for law-giving; 'legislation' keeps the formal, legal register of the Greek.
Clement plays on ἐργάτην (worker) and ἀργὸν (idle); 'idle' preserves the wordplay and the sense of inactivity in true life.
The compound with συν- indicates joint inheritance; 'co-heirs' is the standard rendering and preserves the Pauline echo.

bible_refs.note: πλήρωμα νόμου Χριστὸς εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι

pass_b_english: So Jesus does not rebuke him for failing to fulfill everything in the law. On the contrary, he loves him and defends him for his obedience in what he has learned. But he says he is incomplete with respect to eternal life, because he has not fulfilled the perfect things. He is a worker of the law, but idle in true life. Those things are good—who would deny it? For “the commandment is holy”—but only as a kind of child-leading with fear and preliminary teaching for the one advancing toward the supreme legislation and grace of Jesus. “Christ is the fulfillment of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes” (Romans 10:4). He does not make them slaves, as a slave would, but sons and brothers and co-heirs—those who accomplish the will of the Father.

problems.why: Romans 7:12 says ‘the law is holy’, not ‘the commandment is holy’; the citation is inaccurate
problems.fix: For “the commandment is holy” (citation corrected or omitted, e.g., “as Scripture says, the commandment is holy”).

fixed: Removed the inaccurate citation (Romans 7:12) from the quotation of 'the commandment is holy'; the source simply quotes the phrase without a specific reference.

problems.quote: he loves him and embraces him warmly for his obedience
problems.source_quote: ἀγαπᾷ καὶ ὑπερασπάζεται τῆς ἐν οἷς ἔμαθεν εὐπειθείας
problems.why: Greek says Jesus defends/protects him, not embraces warmly; the nuance changes the action attributed to Jesus.
problems.fix: he loves him and defends him for the obedience he has learned
problems.ruling: ὑπερασπάζεται means 'defends/protects zealously,' not 'embraces warmly'; mistranslates Jesus' action.

edits.old: he loves him and embraces him warmly for his obedience
edits.new: he loves him and defends him for his obedience

fixed: Corrected 'embraces him warmly' to 'defends him' because the Greek 'ὑπερασπάζεται' means to defend or protect, not to embrace warmly.
